what_this_is: a REAL entry in the REAL public-good Rekor transparency log
a real RFC 6962 inclusion proof against a real signed tree head
a real Signed Entry Timestamp under Rekor s own published log key
independently re-fetched by UUID and byte-identical
what_this_is_NOT: NOT a Fulcio keyless ceremony — the signer is a self-managed ECDSA P-256 key
NOT proof of who holds that key: a bare public key resolves no principal
NOT proof of durable continuity — one log entry is one moment
why_a_self_managed_key: Fulcio keyless signing requires an interactive OIDC flow that no offline reproduce can perform. Rather than fake one, this ceremony uses a self-managed key and states the difference. For a stage about submitter identity the substitution is instructive rather than merely acceptable: it isolates binding from resolution, which is precisely 5P s thesis.

axis_authority.resolution: unresolved — nobody vouches for the key holder
axis_authority.continuity: ephemeral — a single entry is a single moment
axis_authority.role: unproven — a log says nothing about authority to act

private_key_disposition: generated in a session scratchpad, NEVER committed, not required to verify
